- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.3), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to account for risk reversal or panic-driven rebound.
- Model consistently overreacts to recent price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days) — cap forecast increase to 2–4% after spike, then allow gradual mean reversion.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive within 3–5 days, model often lags — forecast should be adjusted upward by 1–2% in the following 2–3 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate in high-sentiment periods — add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast if sentiment > 0.6 over last 5 days.
- If sentiment is flat or neutral (0.3–0.6), model shows persistent bias — apply mean reversion correction: forecast = 0.85×previous + 0.15×true if no recent spike.
- Avoid overfitting to recent history — if last 3–5 days show volatility, reduce forecast sensitivity to short-term moves; use 3–5 day moving average for smoothing.
